text: Which expressions obtain a code which outputs ## to the screen? (Original task: drag and drop the conditional expressions into the two gaps; some boxes are not used. Boxes: shift = 2, shift < 0, shift > 2, shift =< 2.)
explanation_en: Let's analyze all possibilities step by step: the shift variable is assigned with an integer value equal to 7 – by no means 9! The expression shift =< 2 cannot be taken into consideration as there is no operator like =< – such a phrase will provoke a SyntaxError exception. The expression shift = 2 looks better, but cannot be used in this context, as we want to perform a comparison, not an assignment – Python's reaction will be the same as described above. Putting the expression shift > 2 after the if keyword will cause the code to output only one hash, so the only location in which we should place it is the box after the elif keyword.

text: What happens when the user runs the following code?

options.text: The program outputs one at sign (@) to the screen.
The program enters an infinite loop.
The program outputs three at signs (@@@) to the screen.
The program outputs two at signs (@@) to the screen.

explanation_en: As the power variable begins its life with the value of 1, the control smoothly enters the while loop. Next, the power variable is incremented (it's 2 at the moment) and one @ is emitted. The loop's second turn causes the variable to be incremented again, and this is the moment when the break instruction goes onto the stage – the loop is terminated and the else: branch is executed. In effect, the second (and at the same time the last) @ is printed.
